Let \(V\) be the \(4\times 6\) matrix with columns \(v_i\), and let
\[
G=V^T V.
\]
Then \(G\) is the Gram matrix of the \(v_i\). Since
\[
VV^T=\frac32 I_4,
\]
the nonzero eigenvalues of \(G\) are \(\frac32,\frac32,\frac32,\frac32\), and \(G\) has two zero eigenvalues. Also \(G_{ii}=1\).

Set
\[
P=\frac23G.
\]
Then \(P\) is a rank \(4\) orthogonal projection in \(\mathbb R^6\), with diagonal entries \(2/3\). Hence
\[
Q=I_6-P
\]
is a rank \(2\) orthogonal projection with diagonal entries \(1/3\).

For a \(4\)-subset \(I\), let \(J=I^c\), so \(|J|=2\). By the complementary principal minor identity for projections,
\[
\det(P_I)=\det(Q_J).
\]
Therefore
\[
\Delta_I^2=\det(G_I)=\left(\frac32\right)^4\det(P_I)
=\frac{81}{16}\det(Q_J).
\]

Since \(Q\) is a rank \(2\) projection with diagonal \(1/3\), write it as the Gram matrix of six vectors
\[
u_i=\frac1{\sqrt3}(\cos\theta_i,\sin\theta_i)\in \mathbb R^2.
\]
Then for \(J=\{a,b\}\),
\[
\det(Q_J)=
\begin{vmatrix}
1/3 & u_a\cdot u_b\\
u_a\cdot u_b & 1/3
\end{vmatrix}
=\frac19\sin^2(\theta_a-\theta_b).
\]
Thus
\[
\Delta_I=\frac34\left|\sin(\theta_a-\theta_b)\right|.
\]

So the desired product is
\[
\left(\frac34\right)^{15}\prod_{1\le a<b\le 6}
\left|\sin(\theta_a-\theta_b)\right|.
\]

Now put \(z_i=e^{2i\theta_i}\). Then
\[
|z_a-z_b|=2|\sin(\theta_a-\theta_b)|,
\]
so
\[
\prod_{a<b}|\sin(\theta_a-\theta_b)|
=2^{-15}\prod_{a<b}|z_a-z_b|.
\]

For six points \(z_i\) on the unit circle, the Vandermonde determinant gives
\[
\prod_{a<b}|z_a-z_b|
=
\left|\det(z_j^{k})_{0\le k\le 5,\ 1\le j\le 6}\right|.
\]
Each column has norm \(\sqrt6\), so by Hadamard’s inequality,
\[
\prod_{a<b}|z_a-z_b|\le (\sqrt6)^6=6^3=216.
\]
Equality occurs exactly for a rotated regular hexagon, i.e. when the \(z_i\) are the sixth roots of unity. This also satisfies the tight-frame condition because
\[
\sum_{i=1}^6 e^{2i\theta_i}=0.
\]

Hence the maximum product is
\[
\left(\frac34\right)^{15}2^{-15}\cdot 216
=216\left(\frac38\right)^{15}
=\frac{3^{18}}{2^{42}}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{3^{18}}{2^{42}}}
\]
